title: Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups
statement:
Split the linked list starting at `head` into consecutive groups, taken from the front: the first group holds 1 node, the next holds 2, then 3, and so on. The last group simply takes whatever nodes remain, so it can be shorter than its planned size (anywhere from 1 node up to one more than the group before it).

Reverse the order of the nodes inside every group whose actual number of nodes is even, leave odd-sized groups as they are, and return the head of the resulting list.
constraints: The list has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
notes:
## Intuition

The simple way is to copy the values into an array, reverse the even-sized slices and rebuild the list. Working on the nodes directly needs only a few pointers: the last node of the part already processed (`tail`), the first node of the current group (`first`), and the node just after the group (`after`). The tricky part is that a group's real size is known only after counting, because the last group may be cut short.

## Approach

1. The first group is a single node and never changes, so start with `tail = head` and `groupSize = 2`.
2. While nodes remain after `tail`, walk at most `groupSize` nodes from `first` to count the group's real `length` and find `after`.
3. If `length` is even, reverse the group in place, starting `prev` at `after` so the reversed group's last node links straight to the rest of the list. Hook the new front (`prev`) onto `tail.next`; the old `first` is now the group's last node and becomes `tail`.
4. If `length` is odd, just move `tail` forward over the group.
5. Increase `groupSize` and repeat; return `head`, which never moves.

## Example 1, step by step

`head = [5,2,6,3,9,1,7,3,8,4]`. Group `[5]` is skipped, `tail = 5`. Group `[2,6]` has `length = 2`, so it becomes `[6,2]` and `tail` is the node `2`. Group `[3,9,1]` has `length = 3`; `tail` moves to `1`. The planned size is 4 and exactly 4 nodes `[7,3,8,4]` remain, so they become `[4,8,3,7]` and `tail = 7`. Nothing follows, giving `[5,6,2,3,9,1,4,8,3,7]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each node is counted once and moved at most once.
- Space: O(1): only a handful of pointers.

## Pitfalls

- Decide by the group's actual length, not `groupSize`: a last group of 4 planned nodes holding 3 must not be reversed, and one holding 2 must be.
- Start `prev` at `after`, not `null`, or the list is cut off after the reversed group.
- After a reversal the new `tail` is the old `first`, not the node `prev` points to.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tail` | last node of the groups already processed |
| `groupSize` | planned size of the current group |
| `first` | first node of the current group |
| `after` | node right after the current group (or `null`) |
| `length` | real number of nodes in the current group |
| `prev`, `curr`, `next` | pointers used to reverse the group |
